open_points.subject: MigrationClosure identity
open_points.text: “two records of ‘the migration succeeded at instant T’ would mean the same thing” versus “it is a fact about the store's history”
open_points.question: Do otherwise-equal MigrationClosures in two different store histories represent the same value, or is equality scoped to one store history?
options: Equality is scoped to a store history; closures from different histories are distinct facts even when all stored fields match
MigrationClosure is globally equal by its stored facts, regardless of store history
Store history must become an explicit fact or identity component of MigrationClosure
open_points.default_guess: Treat equality as scoped to the store history without adding a stored history identifier.

open_points.subject: MigrationClosure lifecycle after restore
open_points.text: “absent, then present for the rest of the store's history” and “The restored store begins its own history from the backup”
open_points.question: When the owner restores a backup that already contains the closure, does the new store history begin with the closure already present, inherit the earlier absent-to-present lifecycle as part of its history, or create a new closure at restore time?
options: The new history begins with the copied closure already present
The new history inherits the backed-up history, including the original transition from absent to present
open_points.default_guess: The restored history inherits the backed-up history and closure; restore does not create or change the closure.

open_points.subject: MigrationClosure reference from AuditEntry
open_points.text: M09 says “the migration closure is unique in the instance” while M10 now says “at most one per store history” and R0-89 permits the same instance to import again after restoring a pre-import backup
open_points.question: What is the uniqueness scope relied on when an import audit entry names the MigrationClosure: the instance across all of its restored histories, or only the current store history?
options: Unique only within the current store history
Unique across the instance's entire lifetime, including all restored histories
Audit entries must identify a closure with an additional history identifier
open_points.default_guess: Read the audit reference as unique within the current store history.
